kind: tour
status: approved
buttonLabel: "Peru in 8 days: altitude, Machu Picchu, Titicaca, and optional excursions"
lead: >-
  This eight-day tour of Peru links Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu, and Puno on Lake Titicaca. With frequent transfers, the route moves from the Pacific coast into the high Andes. To choose wisely, understand when acclimatization may be needed, which visits form part of the main itinerary, how Machu Picchu entry is booked, and which excursions can be added on free days.
---

## Peru in 8 days: what you can see without extending the itinerary

The main route begins in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), continues through [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), then reaches [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) before returning to the capital. It is designed for travelers who want to experience key archaeological landmarks, Andean culture, and a day exploring the high-altitude lake.

Eight days is a short period for such a wide-ranging journey. Flights, trains, coaches, and transfers between airports, stations, and hotels take up considerable time. The itinerary therefore includes free days and optional outings: treat them as ways to use available time rather than mandatory visits that have already been paid for.

## How altitude changes along the route

After arriving on the coast, travelers fly to Cusco, at approximately 3,400 meters above sea level. The program allows rest before a city sightseeing excursion. Next comes a journey to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), a return to Cusco, and an overland transfer to Puno for an excursion on the high-altitude lake.

| Stage | Main feature |
|---|---|
| Lima | Rest after arrival |
| Cusco | Altitude of around 3,400 m |
| Machu Picchu | Train and visit to the Inca city |
| Puno and Titicaca | High-altitude lake |
| Return to Lima | Flight and rest before departure |

Consider both the physical demands of excursions and your tolerance for a rapid ascent to altitude. After arriving in Cusco, avoid adding an intense independent walk to the activities already scheduled. If you have medical conditions or concerns about altitude, advice from a doctor before departure is more valuable than generic travel tips.

## Machu Picchu: why tickets and visiting times must be agreed in advance

From Cusco, travelers head toward [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) by tourist train, then use a bus and return after sightseeing. Railway tickets and museum admissions along the route are provided for this stage. However, entry to the archaeological complex itself is governed by official timed slots and visitor circuits. The date, ticket category, and exact sightseeing route must therefore be confirmed before the trip is finalized.

Visiting Machu Picchu and trekking the Inca Trail are different travel products with different permits. A train ticket does not mean that an Inca Trail hike or access to every additional mountain summit is included. Confirm exactly which entry ticket applies to your visit.

Peru's Ministry of Culture regulates availability and ticket sales. On high-demand dates, it is sensible to secure admission before finalizing the other transport connections.

## Cusco to Puno: the journey is a sightseeing day too

A long coach journey of approximately 10 hours is planned between [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and Puno. It includes stops at historical and archaeological landmarks, among them Andahuaylillas and Raqchi, as well as lunch en route. This is a full sightseeing day, not free time between two hotels.

The next day, travelers visit the floating Uros Islands on [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). Reed is traditionally used here to build islands, household objects, and boats. After the boat excursion, the program calls for a return to Puno and a flight to Lima. Allow sensible time to travel from the harbor to the airport and account for weather conditions on the high-altitude lake.

## Free days: distinguishing included visits from optional excursions

Day four is designated as a free day in Cusco, with an option to add the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/). This is a separate extension: [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/), [Urubamba](/peru/place/urubamba/), and [Chinchero](/peru/place/chinchero/) are associated with the proposed additional routes, not mandatory stops for every traveler on the eight-day tour.

Day seven offers free time in Lima. The program lists possible trips to [Paracas](/peru/place/paracas/), the [Nazca Lines and Ballestas Islands](/peru/place/nazca-lines-and-ballestas-islands/), and city excursions. Coastal destinations, particularly Nazca, require careful assessment of driving times and transport arrangements. Attempting several distant outings within a single free day without a separate logistical plan would be a mistake.

The main tour already includes cultural experiences in Cusco, Machu Picchu, and Titicaca. Optional excursions are for those wishing to explore a particular area more deeply; browse [Peru cultural and historical tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/peru/) for ideas.

## What to check about prices and flights

The list of inclusions covers transfers, meals as specified, excursions with a Russian-speaking guide, rail tickets for the Machu Picchu section, and domestic flights Lima–Cusco and Juliaca–Lima. However, the description of day six separately states that air tickets are not included. **This discrepancy needs to be resolved when agreeing the commercial offer**, with an exact list of paid domestic flights.

Additional excursions, airport taxes, excess baggage, and alcoholic and soft drinks are listed as separate expenses. For Machu Picchu, confirm the entrance ticket for the specific date and visiting circuit rather than relying on a general reference to “tickets as per itinerary.”

Once these points are clarified, you can compare the tour with other [Peru itineraries](/peru/tour/) based on actual cost, number of transfers, and included visits rather than simply the lowest displayed price.

## Frequently asked questions about the eight-day Peru tour

### Is the Sacred Valley included in the mandatory itinerary?

Day four is free in the core schedule, while a [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) excursion is offered as a separate module. Its inclusion and terms must be confirmed before booking.

### Can I visit Machu Picchu without reserving an entry time?

No. Visits require tickets for specified dates and circuits. The entry category and time are agreed in advance. A rail ticket does not substitute for admission to the archaeological complex.

### Is the altitude in Cusco and at Titicaca difficult to tolerate?

Altitude is significant, particularly after arriving rapidly from Lima. Rest is scheduled after the flight to Cusco, but individual responses vary. If in doubt, discuss the trip with a doctor before departure.

### Are domestic flights included in the price?

They are listed among the included services, but the description of one day says the opposite. Obtain an unambiguous, agreed list of flights included in your chosen tour option before payment.

### Can Nazca and the Ballestas Islands be added on a free day?

They are listed as possible optional excursions. Combining them depends on travel times, schedules, and the selected logistics. Do not assume all listed outings are included together in one free day.

lead: "Eight days in Peru from Lima to Titicaca: Cusco, the terraces of Moray, Machu Picchu, and the Uros and Taquile Islands. Explore the order of excursions, the high-altitude road journey, English-speaking guides, and separately paid flights."
---

## “Ancestral Energy”: 8 days from Lima to Lake Titicaca

The “Ancestral Energy” itinerary lasts **8 days and 7 nights**. It begins in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), travels through [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), and ends at [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). The focus is Andean history, architecture, and traditions, with a separate day on the lake.

Unlike longer journeys, this tour does not visit Colca Canyon, Nazca, or the Amazon. The purpose of the eight days is to follow the main historic sites in sequence without lengthy detours beyond Puno. Transfers are still intensive, especially on the high-altitude road from Cusco to Puno.

## Day-by-day itinerary

| Days | Main route |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | Lima and Cusco |
| 4–5 | Sacred Valley, Machu Picchu |
| 6–7 | Highlands and Titicaca |
| 8 | Transfer to Juliaca |

In **Lima**, visits to the historic center and Larco Museum are planned. The museum's collection introduces the history of ancient Peru through pottery, textiles, and metalwork, a useful starting point before exploring Inca sites in the highlands.

In **Cusco**, the itinerary includes a city tour and a visit to [Sacsayhuamán](/peru/place/sacsayhuaman/), an archaeological complex with massive stone walls. On day four, the journey enters the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), visiting [Chinchero](/peru/place/chinchero/), [Moray](/peru/place/moray/), and [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/). The following day is dedicated to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/).

Day six is a sightseeing coach journey from Cusco to Puno with stops in the Andean highlands. On day seven, the group ventures onto Lake Titicaca; day eight ends with a transfer to Juliaca airport.

## What makes the Sacred Valley interesting

[Chinchero](/peru/place/chinchero/) combines an archaeological complex, a colonial church, and local textile traditions. [Moray](/peru/place/moray/) is known for concentric terraces that provide insight into ancient Inca agricultural practices. [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/) preserves a substantial archaeological complex and the distinctive plan of a historic settlement.

On this tour, these sites are combined **within a single day**, with a buffet lunch. The itinerary introduces several different aspects of the Sacred Valley but does not provide a separate overnight stay near every attraction. Photographing terraces at dawn or spending hours at one archaeological complex would require a change to the schedule.

At Machu Picchu, you must also account for the specific ticket circuit and entry time. The visit to the complex and lunch in Aguas Calientes are listed among the included sightseeing services, but a general visit does not guarantee access to every optional climb or trail.

## Across the Altiplano: the road and the altitude

After Cusco, the tourist coach heads toward Puno across the Andean Altiplano. The itinerary lists Andahuaylillas, Raqchi, La Raya Pass, and Pucará. The journey is a sightseeing experience in its own right, rather than just a transfer, with stops and lunch among the inclusions.

[Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) lies at high altitude, and rapid changes in elevation can affect how you feel. When arranging a personal schedule, allow time for acclimatization, proper hydration, and manageable exertion. Travelers with health concerns should discuss suitability with a medical professional in advance.

## Uros and Taquile: two different island experiences

Day seven begins at the floating [Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/), where visitors learn about reed construction and traditional boats. A motorboat then continues to [Taquile Island](/peru/place/taquile-island/). Here, travelers discover local culture and weaving traditions and take a walk around the island. The program specifies **lunch at a local community restaurant**.

| Stop | What you will discover |
|---|---|
| Uros | Reed islands and boats |
| Taquile | Weaving and island settlements |

The lake excursion schedule depends on navigation and weather conditions. Confirm island access, crossing times, and the expected return to Puno. The lake outing is part of the included tour; an overnight cruise aboard a vessel is not included.

## What is included and what is paid separately

The description lists a **price of $1,245**. Included services cover hotel nights with breakfast, scheduled excursions and transfers, some lunches, the sightseeing coach from Cusco to Puno, and the trip to Uros and Taquile. An **English-speaking guide** is explicitly mentioned for some excursions; this should not be turned into a promise of Russian-speaking accompaniment.

Separately listed are **air tickets from Lima to Cusco and for departure from Puno**, additional meals and drinks, and tips. When selecting international and domestic flights, remember that the final day ends near **Juliaca** airport, not in Lima. Plan your onward flight accordingly.

For comparison, the [Peru tours catalog](/peru/tour/) includes trips featuring Colca Canyon, festivals, and the Amazon. The [13-day Candelaria Festival itinerary](/peru/tour/peru-inca-empire-candelaria-festival/) additionally explores the celebrations in Puno and the southern coast.

## Frequently asked questions about “Ancestral Energy”

### How many nights does the trip include?

It lasts 8 days and 7 nights. The main overnight locations are associated with Cusco, the Sacred Valley, and Puno.

### Is Machu Picchu included?

Yes, day five is devoted to Machu Picchu. The exact visitor circuit depends on the selected entry ticket.

### Is there time for the islands on Titicaca?

Yes. Day seven is dedicated to Uros and Taquile and the return journey to Puno.

### Are domestic flights in Peru included?

The Lima–Cusco flight and departure flight from Puno are listed separately as excluded costs.

### What language are the excursions conducted in?

The current itinerary specifies an English-speaking guide for some city and cultural excursions. Confirm the language of guiding for each section.

## Traveling to Machu Picchu on the Belmond Hiram Bingham: what the tour includes

**Here, the train is an experience in its own right, not simply a transfer.** The 6-day journey includes [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Travelers reach the citadel aboard the Hiram Bingham with dining-car service, while the city portions of the itinerary include separate gastronomic dinners.

This option makes sense if the style of travel, dining, and historical atmosphere matter to you as much as the archaeological sites. However, **a premium train does not make the entire tour private**: some sightseeing excursions are conducted in groups with English- and Spanish-speaking guides.

## How the Hiram Bingham differs from Expedition

| Train option | Main purpose |
|---|---|
| Expedition | Transport to Machu Picchu |
| Hiram Bingham | A gastronomic travel experience |

The classic [6-day Lima–Cusco–Machu Picchu tour](/peru/tour/peru-lima-cusco-machu-picchu-6-days/) uses an Expedition-class train. This itinerary includes the **Belmond Hiram Bingham round trip**. A brunch and a gastronomic dinner are served on board. The train is known for its heritage-style carriages, restaurant car, and live musical entertainment.

On the Ada Tours itinerary, the Hiram Bingham departs from a station in Urubamba and follows the river valley toward [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The exact boarding point and train timetable depend on the operating service, as the operator offers different routes. Do not apply a departure time from another Hiram Bingham itinerary to your own ticket.

Another important distinction: **a train ticket and an admission ticket to the citadel are separate documents**. This tour lists entrance tickets to sightseeing sites among its inclusions, but the date and permitted Machu Picchu visitor circuit must still be confirmed in advance. Peru's Ministry of Culture restricts visitor numbers through timed slots and approved routes.

## What the other days include

### Lima: colonial heritage and an evening of gastronomy

At the start of the trip, you explore Lima's historic center and Larco Museum. The city provides context for the rest of the journey, bringing pre-Inca Peruvian cultures, the Spanish colonial period, and contemporary Peruvian cuisine together.

**Dinner at Casa Moreyra is included.** It is a restaurant experience in its own right rather than simply a hotel meal. The specific menu and service depend on the restaurant's arrangements and confirmed booking; extra tastings or alcohol should not automatically be assumed to be included.

### Cusco and the Sacred Valley: monuments and local traditions

In [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), the itinerary features a city walk, San Pedro Market, and historic sites. It then continues to [Chinchero](/peru/place/chinchero/) and its textile traditions, the agricultural terraces of [Moray](/peru/place/moray/), and [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/), where Inca architecture survives.

The city inclusions also specify a separate **dinner at MAP restaurant**. Another day includes an excursion to archaeological sites around Cusco, including Sacsayhuamán. Gastronomy therefore complements the cultural program rather than replacing it.

## Guiding and accommodation arrangements

The itinerary's 5 nights comprise one in Lima, 3 in Cusco, and one in the Sacred Valley. The published arrangements include daily breakfast, private airport-to-hotel transfers, a shared transfer to the railway station, group excursions with English- and Spanish-speaking guides, and admission tickets.

**This distinction matters when comparing premium journeys.** A private airport transfer does not mean every excursion is private; an expensive train ticket does not guarantee a Russian-speaking guide. If you require a personal guide in Russian, this should be discussed as a separate adjustment to the arrangements.

Alcoholic and nonalcoholic drinks and tips are listed as excluded expenses. Domestic air tickets are not specified as a separate item among the inclusions even though the journey involves flights; confirm the exact flight arrangements in the final quote and tickets.

## Altitude, season, and tickets: what not to overlook

Cusco stands more than 3,300 meters above sea level, making the altitude change noticeable after a flight from Lima. Even if your main interests are comfortable rail travel and gastronomy, plan your first hours in the Andes with acclimatization in mind. If needed, agree a gentler walking and sightseeing pace in advance.

Admission to Machu Picchu depends on current quotas and entry slots, not solely on seats aboard the Hiram Bingham. For popular dates, coordinate the train, entrance ticket, and sightseeing circuit as a single booking plan. A general-category ticket cannot guarantee access to every part of the complex.

Other [Peru tours](/peru/tour/) are best compared by their actual sightseeing format and included services. On this six-day itinerary, much of the value lies in the journey to Machu Picchu, restaurant experiences, and cultural program, while the need to acclimatize remains common to all routes via Cusco.

## Frequently asked questions about the Belmond Hiram Bingham tour

### Is the Hiram Bingham train included in the tour price?

Yes. The inclusions list a round-trip Hiram Bingham ticket, along with brunch and a gastronomic dinner on board.

### Are all the excursions private?

No. Under the program terms, group excursions are led by English- and Spanish-speaking guides. Airport-to-hotel transfers are specified as private.

### How does this differ from a standard trip to Machu Picchu?

The main difference is the dining experience on the train and separate dinners at Casa Moreyra and MAP. The archaeological destination is the same, but the rail service and the city experiences differ.

### Does a Hiram Bingham ticket grant entry to Machu Picchu?

The train ticket alone does not grant entry. On the Ada Tours itinerary, admission tickets for sightseeing attractions are included separately; the required date, time, and permitted circuit must still be confirmed.

## Who the private “Inca Deluxe” itinerary is for

“Inca Deluxe” is designed for travelers who want to devote **8 days** to Peru's principal historical sites while retaining the character of a private journey. The route begins and ends in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), with its central section exploring the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), and [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/).

The program stands out for its confirmed arrangements: accommodation in 5-star hotels, private transfers, and the Hiram Bingham rail journey to Machu Picchu. However, **the domestic Lima–Cusco–Lima flight is not included** in the tour price. This matters when comparing the total cost with other Peru itineraries.

Unlike a program combining the Andes with Lake Titicaca or the Amazon, this tour concentrates more on Inca cultural heritage and the quality of accommodation within a limited geographical area.

## The value of a stay in the Sacred Valley

After arriving in Cusco, travelers transfer to the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) and stay at Belmond Rio Sagrado. Day three is paced more gently to allow time for acclimatization after the flight. This is a deliberate part of the itinerary: [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) itself lies higher than many parts of the valley, and continuous sightseeing immediately after arrival does not suit everyone.

The next section includes [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/), [Moray](/peru/place/moray/), and [Maras](/peru/place/maras/). The itinerary also includes local handicrafts and a gastronomic stop at Mil Centro. This part of the journey combines Inca architecture, agricultural heritage, and contemporary Andean cuisine.

If ruins and archaeology are your main interests, you can focus on the sightseeing. If food experiences matter most, pay attention to the specific meals and restaurant reservations listed in the itinerary without assuming extra tastings are included by default.

## Why the Hiram Bingham train matters on this tour

Day five is devoted to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). The route follows the Urubamba River, and the rail portion is followed by a transfer to the archaeological complex. A Hiram Bingham ticket is included, with lunch listed on board.

The journey itself becomes a memorable experience. However, a train ticket does not replace an entry ticket for a specific circuit at the ancient city. The date, entry time, and authorized Machu Picchu route must be checked in the confirmed travel documents.

The following day continues in [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), visiting Sacsayhuamán, Qenqo, Qorikancha, and the city's historic architecture. Machu Picchu is therefore not the only focus: surrounding landmarks offer different perspectives on Inca history.

## Service and budget considerations

The price includes 5-star hotels, transfers, meals as specified, guiding, and the Hiram Bingham ticket. A Russian-speaking guide is listed as an option on request. Domestic flights and optional excursions are additional expenses, as are drinks and tips listed among the exclusions.

The duration also deserves attention: 8 days allow time for the main sites around Cusco, but visiting Lake Titicaca, Colca Canyon, or the Amazon would require a different itinerary. Compare destinations in the [Peru tours catalog](/peru/tour/) or among [cultural and historical journeys](/interests/culture-and-history/).

## Frequently asked questions about “Inca Deluxe”

### Is the Hiram Bingham train included in the price?

Yes. Tickets for the Hiram Bingham train to Machu Picchu are included in the price.

### Is the flight from Lima to Cusco and back included?

No. The domestic Lima–Cusco–Lima route is listed among the services paid for separately.

### Is this a group or a private tour?

It is presented as a private journey with personal transfers. Guiding arrangements, including the language, are confirmed in the specific offer.

### Can Titicaca be added to these 8 days?

Lake Titicaca is not part of the approved itinerary. Visiting it would require changes to the duration and logistics, or selection of another [Peru tour](/peru/tour/).

## Peru: the Inca Empire and the Virgen de la Candelaria festival in 13 days

This journey combines historic cities, archaeological landmarks, and a traditional festival in Puno. Over **13 days and 12 nights**, the route passes through [Lima](/peru/place/lima/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), [Colca Canyon](/peru/place/colca-canyon/), [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/), Nazca, and Paracas.

The main distinction from a standard overview trip to Peru is day six, dedicated to **the Virgen de la Candelaria festival**. It features religious processions, music, costumes, and dance groups. Choose departure dates with the festival in mind first, then coordinate flights, the train to Machu Picchu, and overland transfers.

## How the 13 days are arranged

| Days | Main stops |
|---|---|
| 1–4 | Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu |
| 5–7 | Puno, Candelaria, Titicaca |
| 8–10 | Colca, Arequipa, Nazca |
| 11–13 | Paracas and return to Lima |

Day one is spent in Lima. The itinerary then includes sightseeing in the historic center and **a domestic Lima–Cusco flight**, listed among the included services. Around Cusco, the route explores Inca sites, the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), and a day at [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). An **Expedition-class** rail ticket is part of the program.

Day five involves traveling through the Andean highlands to Puno. Festivities are scheduled for day six; day seven introduces [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) and the [floating Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/). The journey then continues to Colca Canyon and Arequipa. The closing days take in the Nazca area, [Paracas](/peru/place/paracas/), and the return to Lima.

This is a busy itinerary with frequent changes of city. The festival day is embedded within a much broader journey across Peru, with participants spending most of the trip outside Puno. Assess travel times and the opportunity to rest after the high-altitude sections in advance.

## Why the Candelaria festival requires special planning

The Feast of Our Lady of Candelaria in Puno is inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. Religious ceremonies and dance performances reflect local Andean and Catholic traditions, with major celebrations taking place **in February**.

Festival attendance is scheduled for day six, and the inclusions specifically list **a festival admission ticket and transfers**. However, exact departure dates are not fixed for the tour. The itinerary name should not be taken as an automatic guarantee of a particular parade or performance on any chosen February date.

When choosing dates, coordinate Puno's events calendar with the Machu Picchu train and roads in southern Peru. Festival streets can be crowded, and organizers establish the order of events. Also confirm the exact performance covered by the included ticket, the seating arrangement, and whether a return transfer to the hotel is organized.

For travelers particularly interested in traditions, it may be useful to compare [festival and event journeys](/interests/events-and-festivals/) and [cultural itineraries](/interests/culture-and-history/), checking the actual days of participation rather than event names alone.

## Machu Picchu, the Sacred Valley, and altitude

In Cusco and the Sacred Valley, you encounter archaeological centers, Inca history, and colonial-period towns. The planned valley route includes [Pisac](/peru/place/pisac/) and [Ollantaytambo](/peru/place/ollantaytambo/), while the main objective of day four is [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/).

Visiting Machu Picchu requires **a ticket for a specified circuit and time slot**. The exact sites accessible depend on the agreed visitor option and current regulations. The Expedition rail class identifies the train service but does not itself determine the visitor circuit within the archaeological complex.

Cusco, Puno, and Andean passes stand high above sea level. Plan for your individual tolerance of altitude, acclimatization time, and physical demands. An itinerary with successive transfers suits travelers ready for early departures, time on the road, and changing weather.

## Colca, Nazca, and Paracas: the final part of the journey

After Puno, the group travels toward [Colca Canyon](/peru/place/colca-canyon/) and [Arequipa](/peru/place/arequipa/), then continues to Nazca. The itinerary describes **a flight over the Nazca Lines lasting approximately 35 minutes**, followed by travel to [Paracas](/peru/place/paracas/).

Two admission fees are listed separately: **$10 for the Nazca national park and $6 for Paracas**. These fees are paid separately, so account for them when budgeting. Day twelve includes the Ballestas Islands and a return to Lima.

This is a substantially different format from a short Lima–Cusco–Machu Picchu journey: natural areas along the southern coast add new transfers and distinct excursion arrangements. If you have less time, compare the [eight-day “Ancestral Energy” program](/peru/tour/peru-ancestral-energy/), which ends at Lake Titicaca and does not include the festival, Colca, or Nazca.

## Tour price and included services

**The tour price is $3,174.** Included services list the domestic Lima–Cusco flight, the Expedition rail ticket, excursions with a Russian-speaking interpreter, meals as specified, a Candelaria festival ticket, and transfers. Hotels may be replaced by properties of the same category, and the order of excursions may change while the program is preserved.

## Frequently asked questions about the Candelaria tour

### When is the Virgen de la Candelaria festival held?

The main celebrations take place in February in Puno. To attend the promised festival activities, the tour dates must be coordinated with the current events calendar.

### Is Machu Picchu included?

Machu Picchu is scheduled for day four, and an Expedition train ticket is among the services. The visitor circuit and entry time are confirmed when the admission ticket is arranged.

### Does the tour visit the Uros Islands?

Yes. Day seven includes an excursion on Lake Titicaca to the [floating Uros Islands](/peru/place/uros-islands/).

### Are all tickets prepaid?

No. The published list separately specifies fees of $10 for the Nazca area and $6 for Paracas. Other services should be checked against the inclusions for the specific departure.

### Is the tour suitable for a first visit to Peru?

Yes, it covers many of the main historic regions, but involves considerable travel and high-altitude sections over 13 days. Consider the physical demands and the suitability of the festival dates before choosing.
